summary: Just-in-time identity bridge: ephemeral AWS/GCP impersonation proxy for LLM infra debugging
description:
Issue summary: Request to create a secure, auditable just-in-time (JIT) identity bridge that allows SRE/infra engineers to obtain ephemeral AWS AssumeRole and GCP Service Account impersonation tokens for debugging LLM serving incidents.

Impact: Several oncall incidents in the last quarter required cross-cloud live debugging (collecting traces, reproducing traffic against dedicated infra). Currently engineers must request long-lived cross-account keys or be added to overly-broad groups. This increases blast radius and slows incident response.

Scope: Build a short-lived impersonation proxy service (internal-only) which:
- Issues AWS STS AssumeRole credentials (duration 15m-1h) to a scoped role with least privilege for diagnostics.
- Issues GCP short-lived impersonated credentials (via IAMCredentials generateAccessToken / generateIdToken) or Workload Identity Federation for temporary access to prod projects.
- Enforces timebound permissions, requires Just-In-Time approval from oncall lead or pagerduty escalation, and logs all token grants to central audit logs.

Requested outcome: Design + prototype the proxy, document playbook for oncall, and pre-provision a small set of narrow roles for diagnostics (logs-read, traces-read, storage-read for specific buckets, monitoring metrics read, and ability to create ephemeral debug compute in a restricted sandbox).

Duration: Initial prototype expected to run in staging for 4 weeks, then gated rollout to prod with canary accounts.

Resources referenced: existing runbooks /confluence/pages/LLM-Debug-Playbook, incident threads in #sre, and prior ticket INT-30421 (trace access request).
requested_permissions: Read-only access to logging, trace, monitoring, and selected storage buckets; no IAM modify or billing access
duration: up to 60 minutes per grant; default 15 minutes; renewable with approval
business_justification: Reduce mean time to resolution for LLM serving incidents by enabling rapid, auditable access for diagnostics while limiting long-lived credentials and scope. This supports faster incident response without broadening permanent privileges.
approval: Requesting initial approval from Security (Niloufar Hosseini) and Oncall Lead (Jamal Reed). Will require secops checklist sign-off before prod rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Aisha Patel: Filed initial request after multiple incidents where engineers had to wait >2 hours for cross-account keys. Attached incident excerpts and list of required read scopes.
2026-03-10 11:03 - Miguel Torres: Acknowledged. Will sketch architecture for a proxy that brokers STS and GCP IAM calls. Want to confirm auditing path (Cloud Audit Logs + S3/Cloud Storage retention).

2026-03-11 08:47 - Niloufar Hosseini (Security): High level OK with JIT approach, but require MFA + approvals and per-request justification that gets stored with the token grant. Also require automatic revocation and periodic attestation for roles created.
2026-03-11 13:22 - Miguel Torres: Noted. Prototype will integrate with PagerDuty approval webhook and internal CA to mint ephemeral certs. Will post design doc to Confluence this week.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Jamal Reed (Oncall Lead): Prefer default 15m duration. Approve narrow diagnostics roles creation in staging for initial testing.
investigation_notes: Reviewed prior requests: INT-30421 shows frequent need for trace read and bucket read; avoid granting s3:* or storage.* broad permissions.
Evaluated existing tools: aws-iam-authenticator and gcloud impersonation exist but require elevated base permissions; wrapper service reduces need for direct privileges.

Prototype options: (A) Lambda-based broker to call STS AssumeRole with approval; (B) Small internal service with OIDC token exchange for GCP. Leaning toward containerized service for better observability.
Audit design: emit structured grant events to splunk/logging with fields: requester, approver, justification, roles_granted, duration, request_id. Store token hashes not raw creds.
Risk notes: ensure no token lifetime >1h; block cross-account role chaining; disable ability to create new IAM principals via proxy.
resolution: In progress: design doc posted at related_confluence_pages. Security pre-approval obtained for staging. Next steps: build prototype (PR linked), run canary in staging (week 1), run tabletop with oncall, then gated prod rollout after attestation. Final resolution will include runbook additions, role enumerations, and automated audit retention policy.
